answer: No. The story is not entirely free of cliches. For example, it uses the very common, overused expression "Es lag Frühling in der Luft" ("Spring was in the air"). Furthermore, the characterization of the protagonist—a well-dressed, energetic young man who arrives at a mountain resort and is immediately disappointed by the lack of familiar society—relies on a very standard trope of turn-of-the-century European literature (the excerpt is actually the opening of Stefan Zweig's famous novella *Brennendes Geheimnis*). While the majority of the descriptive imagery is vivid and poetic, the presence of these familiar expressions and tropes means it is not completely without cliches.
